{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABbmpEeQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhFKN48", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 81, "title": "Reduce CI feedback from ~1 hour with balanced parallel browser shards and early checks (preserve full coverage)", "body": "## Problem and goal

**The current PR/main CI feedback loop takes roughly an hour, which slows development and delays finding failures.** Optimize elapsed *feedback time* without removing important validation, changing numerical/raster thresholds, or weakening GitHub Pages deployment safety.

### Measured evidence (2026-11-01)

| Source | Browser step | End-to-end workflow | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [latest successful main #41304304814](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/41304304814) | **55.15 min** | **~62.97 min** | 102 Playwright tests registered, 100 passed / 2 optional native-WebGPU skips, one worker; build ~1.92 min, `npm test` ~3.97 min, setup/download/deploy comparatively small |
| [0.1.3 PR #41299511791](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/41299511791) | **55.32 min** | ~62 min | successful |
| [Physics PR #41301938061](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/41301938061) | **62.05 min** | ~69 min | browser suite failed *after* nearly an hour; expensive feedback |
| [main #41187194269](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/41187194269) | **33.97 min** | ~38 min | 99 registered cases |
| [historic optimized CI #40814007482](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/40814007482) | **21.33 min** | ~36 min **including optional extra matrix measurements** | historic #54/#57 optimization, 73 cases; not equivalent to current suite |

The recent speedup was real: [PR #57](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/57) reduced redundant Solver/VMD GPU matrices, with matched filtered runs showing ~38–43% improvement. **PR #76** documented test/CI principles but changed **no workflow or test execution**. The later suite grew, and importantly between 10/31 and 11/1 the **97 common passing browser cases alone became ~18.7 minutes slower**, whereas three new Uka error/retry cases added ~2.3 minutes. Same Ubuntu image `20261025.353.1`, Node `v22.23.4`, Chromium `141.0.7390.37`, but different hosted regions/runners. Suspect runner/CPU variability, not proven; measure rather than invent a single cause.

Current bottleneck is [`.github/workflows/pages.yml`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/.github/workflows/pages.yml) running `npm run test:browser` in the **same single `build` job** as `npm ci`, build, typecheck and Node tests, before permitting main deployment. [`playwright.config.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/playwright.config.ts) uses **`workers: 1` and CPU SwiftShader**. Renderer readbacks/synchronization are expensive; historical phase measurements in [`docs/browser-ci.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/browser-ci.md) identify the issue but do not prove all time is shader compilation.

### Relevant three.js practice

- Official [three.js CI workflow](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs Unit/Lint separately and E2E across **five independent parallel Actions jobs**, each with its own runner, while still exercising software rendering. [Recent official successful run #41305009688](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/actions/runs/41305009688) completed 563 screenshots in five shards; slowest E2E job ~10.35 min. **Not directly equivalent work per test** to mmd-gltf's extensive skinning/physics/IK/geometry numerical tests.
- [Three.js PR #34572](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/34572) experimentally moves browser-independent rendering to native Node WebGL/WebGPU and reports further gains; **open/unmerged as checked on 2026-11-01**. Treat as a possible later experiment, not an adopted official baseline and not a prerequisite for this task.

## Required implementation: shorter feedback without weaker gates

### 1. Establish fair, reproducible measurements

- [ ] Read the newest workflow, per-test Playwright logs, and `test-results/browser-summary.json` from actual Actions `browser-evidence` artifacts. Record per-suite and per-case durations, suite size, runner image, Node/Chromium versions, CPU/region where available, cache status, queue delay, full critical path and total runner-minutes.
- [ ] Repeat measurements of an **unchanged commit** (preferably 2+ comparable runs) to estimate hosted-runner variability; avoid attributing 10/31→11/1 speed change solely to 0.1.3 or the three new tests. Keep baseline numbers with timestamp and workflow SHA.
- [ ] Set a **target, not a guarantee**: cut full required PR CI feedback to **approximately 20 minutes or less** if feasible, with early smoke/type/unit failure feedback in a few minutes. Report achieved median/range, worst shard, CI cost, skipped/test failures and limitations. If the target cannot be met without compromising correctness, document the bottleneck and next iteration.

### 2. Parallelize browser validation on independent runners

- [ ] Split the *existing full* Playwright test set into **approximately four parallel GitHub Actions jobs** as a first measured configuration. Use Playwright's supported `--shard=i/n` semantics or explicit stable suite groups with clear coverage mapping. Run **one browser worker per runner** by default, so CPU SwiftShader processes do not contend with each other on the same small host.
- [ ] **Balance by measured elapsed duration, not just number of tests.** In the latest main browser logs, the largest suites include Solver ~6.8 min, body-motion ~6.6 min, Uka ~6.0 min, VMD ~4.9 min, and public-motion ~4.7 min. Check whether built-in test-count sharding gives imbalanced shards; use more suitable measured file grouping or Playwright sharding if needed. Keep each independent test exactly once in aggregate.
- [ ] Preserve test isolation, retries/failure evidence, per-test timeouts and flags (SwiftShader and supported Chromium), both dev/preview web servers (currently fixed ports 43179/43180), asset/provenance checks, and full suite semantics. Separate Actions VMs naturally isolate ports; do not run competing local workers on shared ports/state.
- [ ] Make every shard's error a blocking required failure: **no silent skips, dropped tests, false success from missing artifacts, or permissive `continue-on-error`.** Retain exactly the two documented optional native-WebGPU skips unless hardware coverage is explicitly added separately.
- [ ] Upload uniquely named failure/screenshot/phase/browser-summary artifacts for *each shard*, **including on failure**. Aggregate shard-level test IDs/statuses, durations, attempt counts, failure reasons and outputs; verify no missing/duplicate test IDs and total coverage against an unsharded `--list`. Reuse existing [`tools/browser-report.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/browser-report.ts) semantics or adjust it to represent per-shard data honestly.
- [ ] Evaluate the cost trade-off. Four runners may increase total runner-minutes even if wall time decreases; report both. Do not blindly raise `workers` within SwiftShader hosts without resource measurements.

### 3. Make fast feedback and publishing gates correct

- [ ] Separate fast checks (typecheck, Node/unit, smoke integration) from slower render-conformance shards so basic regressions become visible promptly. Determine whether they run in parallel after build or earlier. Keep full regression required before merging/publishing; filtered smoke **supplements** the full suite, it does not replace it.
- [ ] Keep `main` Pages deployment gated on **successful build plus all required validation jobs/shards**, never on build-only or first-completed shard. Validate `needs` and `if` behavior on PR, main push, failure, cancellation, skipped optional WebGPU, and workflow dispatch. Publish the **exact tested commit's** `dist` artifact only after all gates; avoid running another entire browser suite during deployment unless explicitly justified.
- [ ] Ensure artifact packaging and model data are available per shard: current `npm run build` rebuilds manifest-verified Uka/Gene assets, and the source cache is keyed on manifests. Measure whether sharing a validated build artifact via `upload-artifact`/`download-artifact` is cheaper than rebuilding in all jobs. Preserve pinned/source hashes, license notices and built-site asset URLs; don't accidentally deploy stale artifacts.
- [ ] Respect existing `concurrency` cancellation per ref and unusual labeled-event logic; preserve required `workflow_dispatch` and opt-in `browser-performance` matrix replay. Standard PR/main runs must **not** execute the optional full/representative matrix repetitions. Avoid duplicate equivalent PR/push workflows when safe, while maintaining merge-commit/Pages validation.
- [ ] Do not prematurely make doc-only PRs skip mandatory checks without an explicit documented coverage/security review. Any change-based test selection requires a demonstrable nonweakened final gate and an auditable path-to-tests rule.
- [ ] Run a controlled **intentional failing test** in a disposable test branch/PR if permitted to demonstrate fast failure visibility, blocking aggregate result and artifacts; do not modify main or leave an intentionally failing change merged.

### 4. Keep GPU confidence, and scope later experiments separately

- [ ] Retain all important BDEF/SDEF/QDEF, Solver, VMD/VPD, bone/group morph, Physics, Outline, Toon/PBR, source-transport, Uka/Gene real-model, Android-adjacent request/Retry, IK and resource lifecycle browser coverage at **unchanged thresholds**. Preserve independent GPU/readback and pixel-oracle checks; Node-only checks cannot replace uniquely GPU-observable failures.
- [ ] Keep CPU SwiftShader as the deterministic existing reference for this first improvement. Do not require paid GPU hardware or a driver change for the initial CI sharding solution.
- [ ] Document a **separately measured, optional follow-up**: prototype browser-independent native WebGL/WebGPU capture as in three.js PR #34572 or an actual hardware-GPU Actions runner, compare exact pixel/vertex/normal/determinism and shader compatibility. Do not treat that unmerged experimental PR as a fully supported replacement or silently relax tolerances.
- [ ] Test how new public Physics work [Issue #77 / PR #79](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/79) would be assigned to a shard without making it a dependency for this performance issue.

### 5. Validate and document

- [ ] Run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, all required sharded browser tests, `npm run check:links`, and `git diff --check`. Retain original test and deployment security constraints; exercise actual Actions jobs, not only local config parsing.
- [ ] Verify on the PR head and the merged main SHA: all expected jobs run, all shards pass, aggregated evidence is complete, Pages artifact deploys only when every required check succeeds, and optional diagnostics remain opt-in.
- [ ] Update `docs/browser-ci.md`, workflow documentation, Playwright reporter/summary usage and development/review guidance with baseline/new timings, test→shard mapping, total runner-minute cost, how to reproduce a failing shard locally, and the condition for adding/redistributing tests.

## Definition of done

1. **Full existing suite is still run and still blocking**, split across independent runners; no regressions, lost cases, weakened raster/oracle tolerances or mislabeled skips.
2. The CI reports early basic failures without waiting ~60 minutes, and its full required critical path is materially shorter than the measured ~63-minute baseline (target ~20 minutes if supported by real measurements).
3. The measured outcome includes comparable-run variability and both **wall-clock** and **total runner-minutes**, rather than claiming an unverified theoretical 4× speedup.
4. Shard-specific failure artifacts and aggregated completeness checks are usable and auditable.
5. Every main deployment waits for all required checks and publishes the matching tested build.
6. Any native/hardware-GPU experiment is explicitly separate unless proven equivalent; quality and regression confidence are preserved.
